title: Apollo AI - POC scoping (open models)
next_steps: Send benchmark spreadsheet and POC runbook
Provide pricing for Dedicated + burst capacity
action_items: Mateo: email benchmark template and pricing (due 2026-08-03)
Priya: prepare initial model shortlist and quantization options (due 2026-08-05)
Sofia: confirm VPC peering window and provide internal IP allowlist (due 2026-08-02)
Rina: share sample data subset for baseline tests (due 2026-08-04)
summary: POC scoping to evaluate open-model options for Apollo AI's multilingual customer support assistant. Discussed success criteria (accuracy, latency, cost), workload sizing, benchmark plans, model shortlist (Mistral, Llama variants, Falcon, RedPajama), quantization and retrieval augmentation approach, and a 4-week POC timeline. Agreed next steps to exchange benchmark data and schedule infra walkthrough.
transcript: [00:00] Mateo (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros?
[00:06] Rina (Apollo): Hi I'm Rina, head of ML at Apollo, we own the assistant project. Happy to be here.
[00:10] Marcus (Apollo): Marcus, CTO, I'll be joining for infra + timeline questions.
[00:14] Ben (Apollo): Ben, PM for the support assistant product.
[00:17] Priya (Redwood): Priya, SE, I'll drive the technical scoping and benchmarks.
[00:21] Jonas (Redwood): Jonas, solutions eng, focused on integration and latency tuning.

[00:25] Mateo: Great. Goal for today is to scope a 4-week POC focusing on open models — baseline quality, latency, and cost tradeoffs for multilingual support. We'll capture success criteria and a short list of models to test.

[00:40] Ben: Roughly our use case is multi-lingual customer support — English, Spanish, Portuguese, some French. Throughput: about 30 qps peak, average message ~120 tokens. Latency target under 300ms tail ideally under 200ms.

[01:05] Rina: Success criteria: 1) F1/Exact-match on our intent extraction + slot filling test set should be >= 88% relative to current finetuned baseline; 2) latency p95 < 350ms for single-request online path; 3) cost < $0.01 per session on average. Also need the model to handle domain-specific terms (billing, product codes).
[01:35] Priya: Helpful — are you planning retrieval augmentation (RAG) against your internal KB? That changes throughput and latency.
[01:40] Ben: Yes, we expect to use a vector store + top-k retrieval. Typical retrieved fragments 3–5 per query, adds ~50–150 tokens to the prompt.

[01:54] Jonas: For benchmarking we'll instrument two flows: pure LLM intent/response and RAG-augmented response. We'll measure latency cold vs warm (KV cache), p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization and cost per 1k tokens.

[02:15] Marcus: On infra, we prefer VPC peering to Dedicated capacity; security is required — SOC2, SSO, audit logs. We'll check whether Redwood Private is needed but for POC VPC peering to hosted is fine.

[02:30] Mateo: Noted. We'll include connectivity options in the runbook. Now model shortlist — given multilingual and domain needs, we recommend testing an ensemble of open models across sizes: Mistral-instruct-like (7B), Llama-family medium (13B), a larger Llama/Falcon-ish 40B variant, and RedPajama/Meta-style 34B. Priya can articulate tradeoffs.

[02:51] Priya: Yeah, quick tradeoff overview: smaller models (7B) are cheaper and faster but may underperform on domain-specific intents and complex reasoning. 13B medium models often hit a sweet spot for quality vs latency. 34–40B models give best out-of-the-box quality but require quantization to be cost-effective; also need more RAM/GPU and yield higher p95 latency. Some models have better multilingual coverage — Mistral and Falcon show strong multi-language generalization in our experience, Llama-variants can be strong if finetuned/LoRA'd.
[03:30] Rina: For our dataset, domain specificity matters — billing codes, internal acronyms. We can share a 5k example subset to run zero-shot + few-shot evals.

[03:40] Priya: Perfect. For the POC we'll run: baseline (your current finetuned model), Mistral-7B-instruct, Llama-13B-chat (quantized), Falcon-40B-instruct (8-bit), and RedPajama-34B. We'll test both with and without retrieval. We'll also include a quantized Llama-13B 4-bit run to see cost/latency gains.
[04:05] Marcus: Are these all available as open weights? Need to check licensing; some require different compliance. Also we need to know memory requirements to plan Dedicated capacity.

[04:15] Jonas: We'll include exact VRAM reqs per model under the quantization profiles section. Example: Llama-13B 4-bit runs comfortably on a single H100/RTX-style P4d equivalent with ~40GB usable GPU memory after quantization; 40B requires multi-GPU or sharded setup unless you run lower perf 8-bit kernels.
[04:36] Ben: How will you run the multilingual evals? We have translation noise and code-switched messages.

[04:42] Priya: We'll run per-language splits for English/Spanish/Portuguese/French and create metrics per language — intent F1, slot accuracy, and overall answer quality judged by a small human eval on edge cases. We'll report deltas vs your baseline.
[04:58] Rina: For measuring hallucinations, we want a metric — maybe hallucination rate on a curated set and precision for entity extraction.

[05:06] Priya: Agreed — we'll instrument hallucination checks using a set of KB-grounded prompts and flag any unsupported claims. Also we'll log a confidence score distribution to calibrate thresholds.

[05:20] Mateo: On timelines — propose 4 weeks: Week 0 (setup + data exchange), Week 1 baseline runs + infra setup, Week 2 model runs and quantization experiments, Week 3 RAG experiments and tuning, Week 4 final analysis, COST/latency tradeoff recommendations and wrap-up. Is that acceptable?
[05:33] Marcus: Sounds fine. We have a launch deadline in Q4 so POC end of August aligns with our planning.

[05:40] Ben: On success criteria — if a smaller model + RAG matches the baseline quality and meets latency/cost constraints, that's preferred. If not, we'll evaluate larger models with quantization or consider Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput.

[05:55] Priya: We'll also run throughput tests at 30 qps and at doubled concurrency (60 qps) to understand autoscaling behavior and batching effects. We'll capture batching latency vs real-time single token streaming.
[06:10] Rina: Security questions: can logs be turned off? We need audit logs only for errors; customer PII must not be persisted unless encrypted. Also SSO support for your console.

[06:23] Mateo: Yes, Redwood supports configurable retention, KMS integrations for encryption, SAML/SSO and full audit logs. We'll share the SOC2 pack and security whitepaper. For POC we can restrict retention to 7 days and mask PII where possible.

[06:39] Sofia (Apollo): For VPC peering we need a maintenance window, and need to provide an allowlist — I can coordinate with infra team. We might prefer Private deployment later but hosted VPC peering is ok for now.
[06:50] Jonas: Noted. We'll document network ports and IP ranges in the runbook.
[06:57] Ben: Benchmarks — can you share the measurement sheet? We'd like to see cost modeling assumptions (price per GPU-hour, token pricing, overhead).
[07:04] Mateo: Absolutely — action item, I'll email the benchmark spreadsheet with the cost modeling tabs. Priya will include expected VRAM and perf numbers per quantization profile.
[07:13] Rina: Any recommended model to start with if we want the fastest iteration?

[07:16] Priya: Start with Mistral-7B instruct and Llama-13B quantized 4-bit. They give fast feedback loops and often approach baseline on intent tasks. If we need higher quality, move up to RedPajama-34B or Falcon-40B. We'll highlight which models are more likely to need LoRA/finetune for domain terms.
[07:35] Marcus: About finetuning — we don't plan full retrain during POC, but LoRA/lightweight adapters are acceptable. Will Redwood support LoRA workflows in POC?
[07:43] Jonas: Yes, we can run LoRA-style adapter experiments; we'll include a short LoRA pass if time permits (week 3) using your 5k sample.
[07:52] Ben: For evaluation, we also want qualitative examples to show product stakeholders; can you produce a demo deck at the end?
[07:57] Mateo: We'll prepare a short deck with benchmark plots, latency/cost tradeoffs, and recommended model/profile per use-case.
[08:05] Rina: Any gotchas you foresee with retrieval latency? We worry about 150–200ms added latency from our vector DB calls.

[08:12] Priya: We recommend async retrieval plus prefetching and caching of frequent queries. Also prefix KV caching can help for chat contexts. We'll measure cold vs warm retrieval latency and recommend caching TTLs.
[08:25] Marcus: On metrics, can you export token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards? We want to see which intents drive cost.
[08:30] Mateo: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and per-route dashboards; we'll grant you read access to a demo org and show how to slice by intents.
[08:38] Ben: Great. Anything around failure modes? We need graceful degradation options if the model is slow.

[08:44] Jonas: We'll configure fallback policies — lower-cost smaller model fallback and cached templated responses for known intents. Redwood supports automatic model fallback policies in the routing layer.
[08:54] Rina: Good. Budget question — can you ballpark cost for the POC running multiple models for 4 weeks? Even a rough estimate helps us sign off internally.

[09:02] Mateo: Rough back-of-envelope: running 3–4 models with periodic continuous benchmarking on a single Dedicated-like GPU fleet for 4 weeks is typically in the low five figures; we'll provide a detailed estimate in the spreadsheet. If you run heavy 40B experiments it'll push higher.
[09:15] Ben: Ok that helps.

[09:18] Priya: Recap of deliverables we'll send: POC runbook, benchmark spreadsheet with cost model, list of model configs (quantization profiles), sample commands for integration, security docs. We'll schedule infra walkthrough with Sofia.
[09:33] Rina: Sounds good. We'll share the 5k sample and the intent taxonomy by Tuesday.
[09:38] Mateo: Action items logged: we'll send docs and schedule follow-ups. Any final questions?
[09:42] Sofia: No, just confirm the VPC peering window — I'll send available times.
[09:46] Marcus: Nothing else from me.
[09:48] Ben: Thanks everyone, excited to see results.
[09:51] Mateo: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials — end call.
[56:00] <recording end>
